label: def:q-navier-stokes
title: $q$-deformed Navier--Stokes equation
html:
The quantum Euler equation models inviscid flow in the brane fluid. To account for dissipation — the irreversible degradation of coherent vortex motion into thermal fluctuations — we introduce the q-deformed Navier--Stokes equation.

Categorical formulation. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a QOU with substrate parameter q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}), where q > 1. Let \Omega^k(A) be the differential forms on the Frobenius--Hopf object A, governed by the q-exterior derivative d_q \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A) and its adjoint \delta_q \colon \Omega^{k+1}(A) \to \Omega^k(A) under the Frobenius pairing. The q-Laplacian operates as \Delta_q = d_q\delta_q + \delta_q d_q.

The q-Navier--Stokes system is the pair of morphisms in \mathbf{C}:

  \partial_t v
  + \mu \circ (v \otimes \nabla_q v)
  = 
  -\rho^{-1}d_qp
  -  d_qQ_q
  +  \tfrac{1}{2}(1 - q^{-1})\Delta_qv
  +  \rho^{-1}\delta_q\boldsymbol{\sigma}_q,
  \partial_t\rho + \delta_q(\rho \cdot v) = 0,

where:

  • v \in \Omega^1(A) is the velocity 1-form,
  • \rho \in A is the density (0-form),
  • p \in A is the pressure,
  • \nabla_q is the q-connection,
  • \mu \colon A \otimes A \to A is the multiplication on A,
  • Q_q = -\tfrac{1}{2}(1-q^{-1})^2 \Delta_q(\rho^{1/2}) \cdot \rho^{-1/2} \in A represents the quantum pressure,
  • \boldsymbol{\sigma}_q = (1-q^{-1})\rho \bigl(d_q v + (d_q v)^\dagger - \tfrac{2}{3}(\delta_q v)\mathrm{id}_A\bigr) \in \Omega^2(A) supplies the viscous stress,
  • and the dagger (-)^\dagger signals the Frobenius pairing.

The kinematic viscosity \nu_q = \frac{1}{2}(1 - q^{-1}) = \hbar_q/2 stems exclusively from the substrate parameter; it is an induced parameter, not an independent physical constant.

Incompressibility. The constraint \delta_q v = 0 (v \in \ker(\delta_q|_{\Omega^1})) stands in for the classical \nabla \cdot v = 0. The observability condition \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 prevents trivial gauge modes from fulfilling this constraint.
